requirements.evidence: routes/web.php:1307-1345 defines every contracted route and middleware (login/register guest, home auth+verified, logout auth, password reset, signed+throttled verification, resend); app/Livewire/Auth/Login.php:225-255 implements strict e-mail validation, lowercased e-mail+IP throttling, session regeneration and intended redirect; app/Livewire/Auth/Register.php:329-351 creates the unverified user, fires Registered, logs in and regenerates the session; app/Http/Controllers/NewPasswordController.php:140-167 validates token/e-mail/default password rule, rotates remember_token, fires PasswordReset and redirects with status; lang/en/ui.php and lang/pt_BR/ui.php plus phpunit.xml:22-23 cover localization. Edge case: registration keeps the e-mail as typed (Register.php:366) while login matches LOWER(email) (Login.php:271), so unique e-mail is only case-sensitive.

conventions.evidence: Most conventions are met: named-route links/redirects, plain wire:model inputs, a Blade layout (resources/views/components/layouts/app.blade.php), Password::defaults() in AppServiceProvider.php:24-28, CHANGELOG.md:26-28, and tests throughout. Deviations: Register.php:362-370 validates through a protected rules() method instead of #[Validate] attributes (Login.php:225-232 uses #[Validate]); form-field markup is duplicated instead of extracted into a Blade component; README/docs were not updated beyond CHANGELOG.

security.evidence: No weakness found. All input is validated server-side (Login.php:236, Register.php:337, PasswordResetLinkController.php:193-195, NewPasswordController.php:142-146); sensitive actions are rate-limited (Login.php:282-298, Register.php:372-388, routes/web.php:1315-1317,1338-1344); verification uses signed + throttled routes and EmailVerificationRequest authorization (routes/web.php:1338-1340, VerifyEmailController.php:75-82); sessions are regenerated on login/register (Login.php:252, Register.php:349) and invalidated with CSRF rotation on logout (LogoutController.php:102-107); all output uses {{ }} and there is no raw-output directive.

tests.evidence: tests/Feature/Auth/{Login,Register,PasswordReset,Verification,Logout,Localization}Test.php cover happy paths, validation failures, rate limits, remember_token rotation, password confirmation, tampered verification id and already-verified resend. Gaps: no unauthorized-call/tamper tests for the Livewire Login::submit() and Register::submit() actions (LoginTest.php:1409-1488, RegisterTest.php:1654-1773), no register guest-redirect or register session-regeneration assertion, and LogoutTest.php:1502-1510 does not assert session invalidation or CSRF token regeneration.

simplicity.evidence: The implementation is direct and reuses Laravel's Password broker, events and middleware; no service/repository layer. Duplication: lang/en/ui.php:537-566 and lang/pt_BR/ui.php:645-674 return the same auth arrays twice under ui.auth and ui.verification, and the repeated label/control/error markup in resources/views/livewire/auth/login.blade.php:31-64 and the other auth views could be a small Blade component.

readability.evidence: Names and methods are clear and small (Login::attemptAuthentication, Register::throttleKey, NewPasswordController::store). Minor issues: ui.login.title and ui.register.title are unused, so Livewire pages fall back to config('app.name') at resources/views/layouts/app.blade.php:961; the controller uses ui.auth.verify_email.sent while views use ui.verify_email.*; public submit() methods have no PHPDoc.

scope.evidence: Every file serves the auth/localization task. The existing welcome and bulma-test views were refactored to route() + ui.* translations (resources/views/welcome.blade.php, resources/views/bulma-test.blade.php) because the task explicitly applies those conventions to existing views. No unrelated features, dependency changes or operations docs were added.

issues.explanation: Registration stores the e-mail exactly as typed while login falls back to LOWER(email), so on a case-sensitive database two accounts differing only by case can coexist and the fallback first() can select the wrong account; normalize the e-mail or enforce a case-insensitive unique rule.

Validation is defined in a protected rules() method instead of #[Validate] attributes on the public properties, unlike Login and the project's stated Livewire pattern (the security policy permits rules(), but the project convention is #[Validate] + $this->validate()).

The Livewire Login::submit() and Register::submit() actions lack the unauthorized-call and tamper tests required by the project's Livewire policy, and RegisterTest never checks that authenticated users are redirected away from /register.

The auth translation arrays are returned twice under ui.auth and ui.verification, and the controller uses ui.auth.verify_email.sent while views use ui.verify_email.*; the aliases are unnecessary duplication and leave dead keys.

Livewire login/register pages never set a localized <title>, so ui.login.title and ui.register.title are unused and the browser tab falls back to the app name while the rest of the page is translated.
The same label/control/error field markup is copied across four auth forms instead of being extracted into a small Blade component, contrary to the project's Blade-component guidance.
The logout test only asserts the redirect and guest state; it does not assert that the session was invalidated or the CSRF token regenerated, both explicit requirements of the logout flow.

review.summary: The change adds a complete Livewire/Bulma session-auth flow with pt-BR localization, signed e-mail verification, password reset, and rate limiting, and it matches the route/component contract. It is well tested and secure overall; the score is held at 4 by a case-sensitivity mismatch between registration and login, a Livewire validation-pattern deviation in Register, and missing tamper/unauthorized tests for the Livewire actions.
